correctness.rationale: For each additive character χ of A=F_p^d, direct two-coset Fourier transformation of the left-regular action yields one 2×2 fiber Bχ=[[Rχ,Fχ],[conj(Fχ),conj(Rχ)]] (up to harmless conjugation/reindexing), across N characters, with det Bχ=|Rχ|²−|Fχ|². Mixed 2+1 coset support is singular precisely when χ(a−b) is a primitive third root; the singleton forces each such block rank 1. For all-in-one-coset triples the block vanishes precisely when their 3 character values form {1,ω,ω²}, with each zero block contributing 2 dimensions. Since each χ-value is a p-th root, vanishing is impossible unless p=3. For p=3 the number of χ with χ(v)=ω or ω² for nonzero v is 2N/3; with independent v1,v2 giving the two target pairs it is 2N/9. This proves mixed nullity 2N/3, collinear single-coset 4N/3 and noncollinear 4N/9. The combinatorial counts are 2*binom(N,2)*N=N²(N−1), 2*binom(N,2)/3=N(N−1)/3, and 2*binom(N,3)−N(N−1)/3=N(N−1)(N−3)/3. These sum to binom(2N,3). For p=2, inversion acts trivially but the same two-coset Fourier decomposition applies; for d=1 the noncollinear stratum is empty. Full proof is analytic for every prime p and integer d>=1.
residual_risks: The source script uses modular ranks, which are consistency checks, not certificates of all complex ranks.
The general kernel fiber reconstruction is fixed by choice of χ and complex-conjugation convention but dimension statements are invariant.

verification.limitations: Tests over Q are exact for the finite cases but do not prove the quantified result for all p,d; theoretical character proof independently assessed.

evidence: Arezoomand–Taeri Corollary 7: characteristic polynomial factors over irreducible representations for any Cayley digraph; Corollary 9 treats cyclic index-two subgroup.
Al-Tarimshawy–Siemons Theorem 1.4 gives a cyclotomic divisibility singularity criterion for ordinary cyclic dihedral Cayley graphs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The representation factorization covers much broader groups but is a generic computation method, not an explicitly quantified support-dependent rank distribution. To imply this result with its multiplicities one must additionally derive the root-of-unity vanishing characterization and count independent linear forms, affine lines, and mixed cosets. All symmetric cyclic special cases covered in earlier theorems are treated as prior; the novel assessment is the complete all-support uniform classification/census, not the block method itself.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A zero eigenvalue of the three-generator Cayley (di)graph, noninvertibility of a three-term group-algebra element, and a nonzero kernel of the three-tap left-convolution operator are equivalent statements. The 2013 full-characteristic-polynomial formula establishes the general block method; its published formula does not evaluate all arbitrary three-tap support classes and their frequencies for noncyclic F_p^d. The 2016 and 2020 cyclic-dihedral analyses concern undirected inverse-closed Cayley graphs (and the latter also connected generating sets), whereas the claim includes identity-containing, directed and nongenerating supports. The separate abelian three-sparse Fourier support spectrum lacks the mixed-coset two-by-two determinant mechanism. No inspected equivalence covers the entire census.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: the general finite Cayley Fourier block method is known (Arezoomand–Taeri 2013), and ordinary inverse-closed cyclic-dihedral cubic formulas are known (Huang–Huang–Lu 2016; Al-Tarimshawy–Siemons 2020). The distinct all-support, all-dimension prime-three nullity trichotomy plus labeled support multiplicity census was not contained in any inspected prior statement. Published elementary-abelian three-sparse Fourier support spectra and ternary Heisenberg support census are adjacent but not logically equivalent. The exactly matching search result is this assessed record, not independent prior art; search absence alone is not novelty proof.

value.rationale: Convolution rank is a natural linear-algebraic/harmonic invariant of a finite group, measuring loss of information under a sparse translation filter. This result gives a complete, size-uniform classification for *all* unordered unweighted three-point supports on the elementary generalized dihedral family, identifies a sharp p=3 obstruction (all three-tap filters singular at p=3, all invertible otherwise), and provides exact kernel dimensions and incidence-geometric frequency counts. The distinction between mixed cosets, affine lines, and independent triples is a motivated structural partition, not an arbitrary small numerical slice; a researcher can directly use the precise rank distribution for sparse group filters. It does not claim a new representation decomposition or generality to weighted/larger-support filters.
residual_risks: Technique uses low-degree character sums and finite-geometry counting; mathematical depth is modest and broader weighted/generalized families remain unclassified.
